key_insight: A quadrature-aware complex-linear neural operator can predict acoustic pressure fields from distributed boundary excitation while preserving the exact linear physics of superposition and zero response to zero input.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster surrogate prediction for resonant acoustics in design, control, and repeated-query workflows where many boundary-source realizations must be evaluated.
method: Uses a complex-linear boundary operator that contracts learned source and receiver bases through explicit surface quadrature.
Represents the vibrating boundary with coordinates, normals, and quadrature weights instead of a fixed flattened sensor vector.
Trained and evaluated against a 3D MRT lattice Boltzmann reference dataset with comparisons to a complex DeepONet.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, CLBO reduced mean complex relative field error to 0.184 ± 0.00771 versus 0.367 ± 0.00742 for DeepONet, with superposition error of 1.31 × 10^-7 and 1.83 × 10^4× faster inference for the reported query size.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate boundary quadrature and solver-to-surrogate data consistency, so performance may degrade if source discretization, geometry, or receiver placement differ substantially from training conditions.
paper_title: Quadrature-Aware Complex-Linear Neural Operator for Boundary-to-Field Prediction in Resonant Acoustics
